audit_scope.basis: Independent review of the supplied function cards and main decision brief. The implementation repository was not supplied; these are oracle cases, not executed application tests.
audit_scope.case_design: Five cases per card: two straightforward, two interaction/complex, one boundary or edge. Conceptual input keys and expected object shapes must be mapped to the real TypeScript interfaces by Claude Code without changing intended behavior.

executive_findings.finding: Missing balance/rate/return must remain distinguishable from numeric zero. pricedGainOf returns null for the whole total if any positive holding has no knowable gain. The card says yearlyInterest returns null for missing rate, while the main brief says annual interest is counted as $0 and disclosed; verify this helper-vs-display distinction rather than flattening unknown into a known 0% yield.

Maturity, missing face/rate, bank-versus-broker CD treatment, priceAtYield, accrued interest and summary reconciliation interact. Exact pricing/sensitivity outputs require real helper execution; do not replace source conventions with a generic bond calculator.
CD detection must ignore institution; money-market funds are Stocks / Funds, not cash; unclassified alternatives remainder is not “other” and must not receive a rate.

Window start, transaction category mapping, known-gain coverage, recorded investment dates, synthetic closing snapshot and no-return reasons need integrated regression tests. DEC-2440 says every return is time-weighted; this part covers adjacent support functions, not the full return engine.
Mortgage/property mapping must not guess when ambiguous. Rent entries without a property identifier are excluded; primary-home fallback is conditional, not universal.
Plural word allow-list, timezone-independent date formatting, tax wording overrides, empty state null semantics, and strict rent parsing have explicit boundary conditions.

cards.name: bondRateSensitivity
cards.what_it_is_for: What happens to this bond if interest rates move?
cards.formula_in_words: Nothing for a CD bought from the bank (pricedLikeBond says no; a CD bought through a broker is priced like a bond, DEC-3837, 2026-10-10), when the yield to maturity is unknown, when the bond cannot be priced (matured or no date), or when the face value or rate was not entered or is zero or less. For rates one percentage point UP and one DOWN: the change = priceAtYield at the yield to maturity plus or minus one point (never below 0.01%) less priceAtYield at the yield to maturity itself. The new price = today's value + that change. It gives a range from 1% under to 1% over the new price, and the change, each rounded in proportion to the bond: to the nearest $1,000 for a bond worth $100,000 or more, the nearest $100 from $10,000, the nearest $10 from $1,000, and so on down.
cards.handed: export function bondRateSensitivity(b: BondInfo, now: Date = new Date()): RateSensitivity | null
inputs_it_reads: MK-XS-I-049 bond price — what the bond is worth today

figures_it_feeds.what_it_answers: Roughly what this bond would be worth if interest rates moved one percent either way.
figures_it_feeds.when_it_refuses: Refused for a CD bought from the bank, for a matured bond, and for anything with no coupon or no maturity — and for a bank CD it says plainly why nothing happens.

rules.words: An estimate, and it wears the estimate label.
FOUNDER 2026-09-27: a CD bought from the bank gets no estimate. It is not traded, so its value does not move with rates; the screen says that instead.
DEC-3837, 2026-10-10: a CD bought through a broker trades, so it gets the estimate like a bond. A CD whose answer was never given is read as bought from the bank.

cards.formula_in_words_reviewed: Nothing for a CD bought from the bank (pricedLikeBond says no; a CD bought through a broker is priced like a bond, DEC-3837, 2026-10-10), when the yield to maturity is unknown, when the bond cannot be priced (matured or no date), or when the face value or rate was not entered or is zero or less. For rates one percentage point UP and one DOWN: the change = priceAtYield at the yield to maturity plus or minus one point (never below 0.01%) less priceAtYield at the yield to maturity itself. The new price = today's value + that change. It gives a range from 1% under to 1% over the new price, and the change, each rounded in proportion to the bond: to the nearest $1,000 for a bond worth $100,000 or more, the nearest $100 from $10,000, the nearest $10 from $1,000, and so on down.
cards.findings: High-risk: rounding scale wording is ambiguous at thresholds; clarify whether “nearest $1,000 from $100,000” applies to range endpoints and delta separately. Broker-CD eligibility and bank-CD refusal must match DEC-3837. The supplied card is a specification, not implementation evidence; run against source before calling this a reproduced bug.

cards.name: priceAtYield
cards.what_it_is_for: Price the bond's future cash flows at a given annual yield (yearly approximation).

cards.name: categoryEarnings
cards.what_it_is_for: What each category of investment paid in dividends and interest over the period, and that category's return.
cards.formula_in_words: Uses the dividend and interest records dated on or after the period's first day, amounts taken as positive. A record that names a ticker goes to that holding's category: bond → Bonds & CDs; cash → Cash in this account; anything else → Stocks / Funds; a ticker with no holding on record → Stocks / Funds for a dividend, Bonds & CDs for interest. A record that names NO ticker → Stocks / Funds for a dividend; for interest, Bonds & CDs when the record's account is a bond or CD account handed in, else Cash in this account. A category's return, over the holdings with a value above zero and a period return above −100%: each holding's value at the start = its value now ÷ (1 + its return over the whole period, never a yearly rate); return = the values now added up ÷ the values at the start added up − 1. Nothing when no holding qualifies. Bonds & CDs shows a stated YEARLY rate instead — each bond account's rate weighted by its balance — when every bond account with a balance states a rate and no bond is held as a holding. On day one all three categories are returned with no return; any other day only the categories that earned more than zero.

MK-XS-I-055 the wrapper an account sits in — ISA, 401(k), IRA and the rest

cards.name: pricedGainOf
cards.what_it_is_for: What the holdings gained over the period in dollars: the true gain for a holding bought inside the period, the price move's share of today's value for one with a price history, the stated rate's share for a CD — and nothing (unknown) when any holding has neither.
cards.formula_in_words: Each holding's gain over the period, added up. For a holding bought inside the period: its whole gain (value − cost). For any other holding with a period return: value × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + return)) when its value is above zero, which is today's value less its value when the period opened; nothing when it holds nothing. For a holding with no period return that states a yearly rate (only a certificate of deposit is given one): value × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + rate) to the power years), years handed in (none handed in counts as 0, so it gains nothing). Any other holding that holds something (its value, or the broker's last price × its shares, or the value it was entered at, above zero) has a gain that cannot be known: the answer is then NOTHING — not zero — for the whole total. A holding that holds nothing gains nothing. (Owner decision DEC-3656, 2026-10-09.)

cards.formula_in_words: Groups the accounts for the Net worth list, by asset-class label or by institution. By class: an account with a class split (accountClassBreakdown) is a row under EVERY class it has a part in, at that part; any other account is one row, whole, under its one class. Each group's total = its rows added up (his ruling, 2026-10-07: the rows under a heading add up to the heading). By institution (an account with no institution goes under No institution set; names are matched trimmed, capitals ignored, and the group shows the first spelling seen): each account is one row at its balance, a group's total = those balances added up, and the group lists the classes inside it with their totals, from the same split, largest first. Group totals by class equal the class rows; both views add to everything owned.

cards.name: whyNoReturn
cards.what_it_is_for: WHY A RETURN CANNOT BE MEASURED, in words a person reads.
cards.formula_in_words: The sentence shown where a time-weighted return cannot be measured; empty when it was measured. Money moved on a day with no recorded value: names the day and says a return cannot be measured across it. A movement with no date: says so. A deposit or withdrawal with no amount on record: names the day and says a return cannot be measured across it. Shares moved in or out: names the day and says the records do not say what they were worth. Nothing to grow from on a day (the previous evening's value + money added − money taken out is zero or less while that day holds a value): names the day and says which — a value recorded with nothing there the evening before and no money added, or more money taken out than was there the evening before plus the money added that day. Since DEC-4439 (2026-10-11) a value below the money added is a loss, measured, and has no sentence. Nothing invested over the period: says there is no return to state. Today's value not on record: says so. A beginning that cannot be read has no sentence here — the period is shown as not covered instead.

cards.formula_in_words: Properties = the accounts whose class is real estate. Mortgages = the debts whose type is mortgage. Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "It is feasible to have property without mortgage but no mortgage without property. So check should be 3 properties in NW - 3 or less mortgage." A mortgage is on the property it names, when that property exists and has no mortgage placed on it yet. A mortgage that names no property is placed only where there is one answer: first, on the one property without a mortgage whose name its own name begins with; then, when exactly one property is still without a mortgage and exactly one mortgage is still without a property, on that property. It gives: the count of properties and of mortgages; for each property its mortgage (or none) and that mortgage's required monthly payment; the mortgages on no property; whether there are none of those; and the sentence to show when there are.

cards.name: altPartsOf
cards.what_it_is_for: The alternatives inside one account, each with the kind its yearly rate is read from.
cards.formula_in_words: The alternatives inside one account, each with the kind its yearly rate is read from. An account that is itself an alternative: its alternatives part of the class split (or its whole balance when it has no split), at its own kind. Any other account: each option at its synced value, kind options; each holding classed as an alternative with a price, shares × price, kind crypto when its name says bitcoin, ethereum or crypto, commodities when it says gold, silver, platinum, palladium or commodity, otherwise other; and whatever of the account's alternatives part is left (more than half a cent either way) is a part with no kind, marked asset type not classified — never other, and given no rate (DEC-4036h, 2026-10-10). Nothing when the account holds no alternatives.

cards.what_it_is_for: DEC-3768c (2026-10-10): a rent figure with words in it is not read — it counts as not entered, never as the digits inside it ("about 2k" was $2 and made the property a rental).
cards.formula_in_words: A rent figure as a number. Owner rule, 2026-10-10: a rent figure is a number. It is read only when it is a plain number: digits with at most one decimal point, allowing a leading dollar sign, thousands commas and spaces. A figure with letters or any other text in it (a word such as "about", a "k" for thousands, "n/a", a minus sign) is not read and counts as not entered, never as the digits inside it. Not entered, blank or missing gives 0.
